note.question: How does demand learning affect utility fairness in contextual dynamic pricing?
note.overview: This paper introduces a novel contextual bandit algorithm for personalized pricing under utility fairness constraints in scenarios with uncertain demand, achieving an optimal regret upper bound. The paper's approach, which incorporates dynamic pricing and demand learning, addresses the critical challenge of fairness in pricing strategies. We first delve into the static full-information setting to formulate an optimal pricing policy as a constrained optimization problem.

components.formal: Algorithmic rule: At a higher level, Algorithm 1 can be divided into two phases.
conditions: The first phase consists of T0 = ⌈T2=3⌉time periods, during which price experimentation is carried out by offering nonpersonalized fixed price to all incoming customers, at one lower price pL and one higher price pU.
In the algorithm, the two prices are set as pL = p and pU = p, but they can be changed to any pair of prices in [p,p] that are not too close to each other.

After the price experimentation phase ends and observations are collected, a maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) procedure is carried out to obtain estimates bθ, bα of the unknown model parameters θ0,α0.
